title: Meeting room booking capstone
idea: The capstone is one system you design end to end, a meeting room booking service, grown page by page from requirements to a design you defend.
points: You build one system across the chapter: the Meeting Room Booking System.
The must-haves: search free rooms, book, cancel, no double booking, notify attendees.
Each must-have gets one owning class, so scope and design stay traceable.
Recurring bookings are a stretch goal; finish the must-haves before touching them.

items.label: Requirements
items.text: Turn the brief into use cases and entities: Room, Booking, Employee, Building.

items.label: Class design
items.text: Draw the class diagram and fix the interfaces before writing any logic.

items.label: Core build
items.text: Implement BookingService on top of two repositories and a ConflictPolicy.

items.label: Hardening
items.text: Add error codes, logs and counters, then patterns and tests.

items.label: Review and present
items.text: Refine after peer review, document with UML, and defend each choice.

code.title: Scope with owners
code.caption: The brief as data: every requirement has a priority and an owning class.

walk.text: Each requirement names its owner: the class that will answer for it.
An `enum` makes priority a closed set: must-have or stretch.
A `record` holds one requirement; its `toString` prints one tidy line.
Looping over `Priority.values()` lists the must-haves first and the stretch goal last.

pitfalls: Do not write classes before the must-have requirements are written down and agreed.
Avoid starting recurring bookings early; they reshape the overlap rules everything uses.
Keep the core class names fixed; renaming midway breaks every later step.

options: Requirement[id=R4, text=no double booking, priority=MUST, owner=ConflictPolicy]
quiz.why: The record overrides `toString`, so `println` uses that method instead of the generated `Requirement[...]` form.

takeaway: One system, fixed names, must-haves first, each requirement owned by a class.

starters: Why does every requirement need an owning class?
How do I decide what is a must-have and what is a stretch goal?
